_about: Recorded LLM generations + judge verdicts produced by Claude (Anthropic) using the same prompts the code sends. Served by the 'replay' provider so the evaluation runs offline and reproducibly. Structural Soundness is still computed live in Python over these emails; Fact Faithfulness and Tone Alignment use these recorded judge verdicts.

advanced.S01:
SUBJECT: Following up on our cloud migration conversation
---
Hi Priya,

Thank you for such an engaging conversation today — I really enjoyed getting into the details of your move to the cloud and where you want to take it next.

As promised, I'll send over the technical architecture document by Thursday so you have everything in one place to review. Once you've had a chance to look it through, could we set up a 30-minute scoping call next week to map out the next steps together?

Looking forward to continuing the discussion.

Warm regards,
Daniel Owens
advanced.S02:
SUBJECT: Request for Enterprise Proposal Details
---
Dear Acme Solutions team,

Thank you for the materials shared during our introduction. To advance our evaluation, we would be grateful for some further detail.

Specifically, could you provide full pricing for the Enterprise tier, including any overage rates, together with a copy of your current SOC 2 Type II report for our security review? As our decision deadline is June 30th, an early response would be greatly appreciated.

Please let us know if any additional information would assist on your side.

Kind regards,
Procurement, Northwind Ltd.
advanced.S03:
SUBJECT: ACTION NEEDED: Checkout outage — deployment freeze in effect
---
Team,

Checkout has been failing for customers since 2:10 PM UTC. The on-call team is actively investigating and currently estimates a fix within 30 minutes.

Effective immediately, please freeze all deployments until we issue the all-clear — we need a clean window to verify the fix without introducing new changes.

I'll share the next update as soon as our status changes.

Thanks,
Incident Commander
advanced.S04:
SUBJECT: An apology and an update on your order #48217
---
Dear Mr. Alvarez,

I'm truly sorry for the delay with your order #48217. A warehouse issue on our side held it up, and I completely understand how frustrating it is to wait longer than you should have to.

The good news is that your order is now prioritized and will ship within two business days. As a sincere apology for the inconvenience, I'd also like to offer you 15% off your next order.

Thank you for your patience, and for giving us the chance to put this right.

Warm regards,
Customer Care, Brightline
advanced.S05:
SUBJECT: Request to adjust the report deadline
---
Hi Sandra,

I wanted to raise a timing point early rather than at the last minute. The market analysis section needs one more round of data validation to meet the standard we're both after — rushing it risks errors in the figures.

To do it properly, I'd like to request moving that section from Friday to the following Tuesday. To be clear, every other section is on track and I'll deliver those on time as planned.

Happy to talk it through if that's useful. Thanks for understanding.

Best,
Marcus
advanced.S06:
SUBJECT: Introducing your new account manager, Rachel Kim
---
Hi team at Vantage,

I'm delighted to introduce Rachel Kim, who will be taking over as your account manager. You're in great hands — Rachel brings eight years of experience in B2B SaaS onboarding and a real talent for making transitions feel effortless.

So the handover is smooth, we'd love to set up a joint call next Wednesday at 10 AM, where you can meet Rachel and we can walk through everything together. Nothing about your service will miss a beat.

Please let us know if that time works for you.

Warm regards,
Tom Becker
advanced.S07:
SUBJECT: Reminder: Invoice #1043 is now 30 days overdue
---
Dear Accounts Payable,

I'm following up on invoice #1043 for $4,200, which was due on May 15th and is now 30 days past due.

We value our relationship and would like to resolve this promptly. Could you please arrange payment, or send a status update, by the end of this week? That will allow us to avoid applying the late fee set out in our terms.

If there's any issue with the invoice itself, let me know and I'll be glad to help sort it out.

Kind regards,
Lena Fischer, Finance
advanced.S08:
SUBJECT: Thank you — your talk was the highlight of the day
---
Dear Dr. Osei,

Thank you so much for joining us — your session on resilient leadership was a genuine highlight and drew the highest engagement of the entire day.

The impact was obvious: several attendees came up afterward asking for your slides, which says everything about how much your message landed. Whenever you have a moment to share them, we'll gladly pass them along.

We'd be thrilled to have you back for next year's summit. Thank you again for making the day so memorable.

With appreciation,
Events Team, Horizon
advanced.S09:
SUBJECT: Following up on your partnership proposal
---
Hi Elena,

Thank you for sharing your partnership proposal, and for the thoughtful conversations that led up to it. Our team was genuinely impressed by your analytics platform — you've clearly built something strong.

After careful consideration, the proposed integration doesn't fit our current roadmap, so we won't be moving forward at this stage. I'd rather be straightforward with you than leave you waiting on a maybe.

That said, our priorities shift each year, and I'd welcome the chance to revisit this in Q1. I'll reach out then — and please don't hesitate to do the same.

With respect,
Partnerships, Cobalt
advanced.S10:
SUBJECT: You're invited: early access to our new analytics dashboard
---
Hi there,

Because you're one of our most valued customers, we wanted to give you something before anyone else hears about it. On July 1st, we're opening early access to our brand-new analytics dashboard — and we'd love for you to be part of it.

This is a genuinely exclusive group: just 50 spots. In return for your feedback, you'll get direct access to our product team and a 3-month free upgrade as our thanks.

If you'd like one of the spots, simply reply and we'll save your place.

Excited to build this with you,
The Lumen Product Team

S01.reasoning: Warm and personable while staying professional; greeting and sign-off match the requested register well.

S02.reasoning: Appropriately formal and precise without being cold; matches a procurement request.

S03.reasoning: Conveys urgency through the subject and directive, yet the body stays measured and calm — exactly the brief.

S04.reasoning: Genuinely empathetic and sincere; acknowledges the customer's frustration before the remedy.

S05.reasoning: Professional and clearly accountable — owns the cause and reassures on the rest of the work.

S06.reasoning: Friendly and reassuring; the 'nothing will miss a beat' line directly addresses client anxiety.

S07.reasoning: Firm and clear on the overdue amount while remaining courteous; could be marginally warmer in the open.

S08.reasoning: Appreciative and enthusiastic; specific praise makes the thanks feel earned rather than generic.

S09.reasoning: Diplomatic and respectful — declines clearly but softens with genuine praise and a concrete door left open.

S10.reasoning: Exciting and exclusive in feel; strong, though the exclusivity could be pushed a touch further.

S01.reasoning: Professional and complete but a little stiff for a 'warm' follow-up; generic 'Follow Up' subject and formal 'Dear' flatten the warmth.

S02.reasoning: Suitably formal, though the 'I hope this email finds you well' filler is templated rather than crisp.

S03.reasoning: Reads as a routine FYI — it is calm but lacks the urgency the brief calls for; 'Production Issue Notification' undersells the impact.

S04.reasoning: Apologizes but in a formulaic, corporate register ('any inconvenience this may have caused'); misses the sincere, empathetic tone requested.

S05.reasoning: Professional and clear, but transactional — less of the personal accountability the tone asks for.

S06.reasoning: Friendly enough and informative, but the reassurance is thin compared with the brief.

S07.reasoning: Firm but tips into blunt/demanding ('If payment is not received...'), losing the courteous balance requested.

S08.reasoning: Appreciative but restrained — 'very well received' lacks the enthusiasm the tone calls for.

S09.reasoning: Clear but abrupt; the rejection lands flatly with little of the diplomatic warmth requested.

S10.reasoning: Informative but flat — reads like a standard announcement, missing the exciting, exclusive feel.
